content: The court addressed division after community dissolution, focusing on residual community treatment of a current account and an investment fund. The interpretive problem was whether balances in accounts held by one spouse enter the community and at what date and amount. Framed under arts. 177–194 c.c., the court held that unconsumed earnings and balances existing at dissolution enter residual community; the amount present at that date is split equally. Principles: personal tools for professional activity remain personal; residual assets are only what exists at dissolution. The court awarded half of the account balance and denied claims over an enterprise price as personal. Mutual costs compensated. 1.
